# PackMan 1.10 for macOS

This release improves recovery and batch-update reliability, clarifies scan results, and consolidates maintenance code. Windows remains at v1.9.1.

## Reliability

- **Recover in the right environment.** History retries and verification check the original manager executable and runtime search paths. If they changed, PackMan stops with guidance to select the original executable in Sources and scan again. Older history files remain readable.
- **Keep ambiguous packages blocked.** History uses the same installation eligibility checks as the main table. A retry cannot bypass an ambiguous package identity.
- **Refresh managers during a batch.** PackMan rechecks the manager before each package and before verification. Updating npm from 11 to 12 no longer leaves later packages using npm 11's install-script settings.
- **Explain nonautomatic results.** Ignored, manual, skipped, and ambiguous-only results show why no automatic updates are pending. Partial scans still show their issues.

## Maintenance

- One cache-cleanup implementation now handles previews and execution. Coverage includes configured manager paths, output, failures, unsupported sources, and the separate NuGet global-package opt-in.
- macOS CI covers Xcode 16.4 and 26.6, with Swift compiler warnings treated as errors.

## Downloads

- **PackMan-macOS.dmg** — open and drag PackMan to Applications.
- **PackMan-macOS.zip** — unzip the application.
- Both support **Apple Silicon and Intel**, require **macOS 14 or newer**, and include SHA-256 checksum files.

The application is ad-hoc signed. For a first browser download, macOS may require **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** after attempting to open it. Existing installations can use **PackMan → Check for Updates… → Install and Restart**.

Windows downloads remain on the [v1.9.1 release](https://github.com/dklasens/PackMan/releases/tag/v1.9.1).
